      <title>Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities</title>

      <description><p>Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent</p><p>Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.</p><p>The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/10/lewis-hamilton-egypt-rafah-crossing-gaza-aid-facilities">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/10/china-green-energy-john-kerry-cop31</link>
      <description><p>Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/live/2026/nov/10/cop31-live-fossil-fuel-carbon-emissions-climate-crisis-latest-news-updates">Cop31 live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>China is leading the world <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/feb/05/china-green-energy-sector-investment-growth">in moving away from fossil fuels</a>, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.</p><p>As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/10/china-green-energy-john-kerry-cop31">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit</p><p>Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case.       <description><p>Hamish Falconer says UK has ‘not accepted principle’ of linking electricity trade to ‘cohesion fund’ but two sides will discuss issue</p><p>Britain is willing to discuss paying towards infrastructure schemes in poorer parts of the EU in return for access to the European electricity market, according to the minister in charge of renegotiating the bilateral relationship.</p><p>Hamish Falconer, the cabinet minister in charge of EU talks, told the Guardian he was sure the two sides would discuss the issue after this month’s summit, as ministers look to deepen ties with the union over the next few years.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/10/britain-eu-electricity-market-cohesion-fund-hamish-falconer">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>New alliance with the Netherlands and Baltic and Nordic countries comes in response to 41% increase in Russian naval activity around UK</p><p>Russian naval activity around the UK has increased by 41% in the first nine months of the year, a British defence minister has said, as the Royal Navy announced plans to step up a 10-country maritime defensive effort in response.</p><p>Luke Pollard, the minister for defence readiness, described the figure as “a huge increase”, justifying a new drone and warship initiative from “the alliance of beer-drinking nations” – the UK, the Netherlands and the Baltic and Nordic countries.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/10/russian-naval-aggression-defensive-initiative-beer-drinking-nations">Continue reading...</a></description>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 06:06:31 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>Teachers divided over compulsory 11 November ceremonies at schools</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261111-teachers-divided-over-compulsory-11-november-ceremonies-at-schools</link><description>
A new government initiative requires primary schools across France to hold ceremonies honouring those who died for the country. But teachers are divided over its purpose and the role of the military in education. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8f4305e2-dd0b-11f1-ad88-012109f6bc5c</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 06:05:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG">REUTERS/Pascal Rosssignol</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students demonstrate solidarity in the fight for better schools</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-students-demonstrate-solidarity-in-the-fight-for-better-schools</link><description>
It began as a protest over crumbling classrooms and missing teachers, but France's student movement is now challenging the political establishment to give young people more of a say in decisions about their future. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f19af422-dc5f-11f1-a6cf-03231484c166</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 21:55:52 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg">AP Photo/Nicolas Garriga - Nicolas Garriga</source><dc:creator>Alison Hird</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French student protests continue amid deadlock over education reforms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-student-protests-continue-amid-deadlock-over-education-reforms</link><description>
Students and teachers are planning a new day of strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday, as talks with the government remain deadlocked, nearly two months after the start of protests by high school and university students.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37288fa8-dcd4-11f1-aace-7ff548d44c0a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 06:59:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner joins race for French presidency</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-olympic-judo-champion-teddy-riner-joins-race-for-french-presidency</link><description>
France's five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's presidential election, expressing concern particularly over "the rise of the far right".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff9ac7be-dc3c-11f1-a6ee-d528d7ed3f40</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:44:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg">© AP - Michel Euler</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM's move to increase minimum wage fails to convince unions</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-pm-s-move-to-increase-minimum-wage-fails-to-convince-unions</link><description>
The French government on Monday announced a 1.6 percent increase in the national minimum wage, alongside a series of measures aimed at easing cost of living pressures. However, the decision fell well short of the demands of trade unions, who have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1fb23d3e-dc42-11f1-9f6d-714e057b766f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:36:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg">© Emma Da Silva/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'I still have nightmares': victim of police violence seeks justice six years on</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-i-still-have-nightmares-victim-of-police-violence-seeks-justice-six-years-on-michel-zecler</link><description>
Three French police officers are due to go on trial on Monday over the brutal beating of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020 – a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police violence and racism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0aa97116-dc27-11f1-890c-17b2c492ee48</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:29:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg">AFP - JOEL SAGET</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mélenchon bets on radical change as French presidential race takes shape</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-m%C3%A9lenchon-bets-on-radical-change-as-french-presidential-race-takes-shape</link><description>
Leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to pursue an uncompromising programme of radical change, as he bids for the French presidency in 2027 – despite warnings that his divisive politics could ultimately hand victory to far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">273d195c-dc1a-11f1-8d60-5f29074843e0</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:01:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg">©  KENZO TRIBOUILLARD / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French food bank donations fall as frequency of use spikes in cost of living crisis</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-drop-in-french-food-bank-collection-as-rising-cost-of-living-hits-donations</link><description>
France’s annual food bank collection has gathered less than expected in the face of the rising cost of living, which has left people with less to spend on donations. The three-day campaign, which ended on Sunday, aimed to collect enough food to provide the equivalent of 20 million meals.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7b3dffa-dc2b-11f1-8a7f-0f7ff0c2412a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:09:22 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg">© Mehdi Fedouach/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French MPs weigh up debate on right-wing TV channel ban as petition tops 1m</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-mps-to-weigh-debate-on-banning-conservative-tv-channel-as-petition-tops-1m-cnews</link><description>
A petition calling for French television channel CNews, often compared to American broadcaster Fox News, to be shut down has received more than a million signatures, two days before lawmakers meet to consider whether a ban should be debated in parliament.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19210fc8-dc0a-11f1-bd4e-25468b64d7d5</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 06:52:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Unions vow to maintain pressure on government after fourth wave of protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261108-unions-vow-to-keep-pressure-on-french-government-after-fourth-wave-of-protests</link><description>
Education union chiefs on Sunday vowed to maintain pressure on the French government after student organisations called for another day of nationwide strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">36cb7bb6-dac6-11f1-b148-e9346ba72bac</guid><pubDate>Sun, 08 Nov 2026 11:00:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg">AP Photo/Emma Da Silva - Emma Da Silva</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>French students vow to continue protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/video/20261107-french-students-vow-to-continue-protests-paris</link><description>
French pupils and students are protesting and blockading schools over poor conditions and a university admissions system (Parcoursup) seen as over-selective and opaque. Despite recent concessions by the government, students at Hélène Boucher high school in Paris say they'll continue, even after riot place were sent to break their blockade.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8c9b5ff0-dab9-11f1-a45a-31b57fcb4ae5</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:02:47 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France braces for second day of protests within 48 hours</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261107-france-braces-for-second-day-of-protests-within-48-hours</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people were expected to take to the streets on Saturday for a day of protests over the poor conditions in schools and the rising cost of living.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33ad1cbc-da96-11f1-8df4-1da1eb33321e</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 12:10:04 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Hannah McKay</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: France's student protests and how they fuelled a larger social movement</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261106-podcast-france-s-student-protests-and-how-they-fuelled-a-larger-social-movement-may-68</link><description>
A look at France's high school protests and how they have fed into an ongoing social movement. What are the students protesting against? What impact has the police crackdown had? How has the government reacted? And a comparison with student movements of the past.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bcd965aa-d9cd-11f1-b272-af07f9a85ea6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:29:10 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French lawyers to sue interior minister over 'mutilation' of young protesters</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-french-lawyers-to-sue-interior-minister-over-mutilation-of-young-protesters</link><description>
Lawyers representing at least 18 people injured during protests in France in recent weeks say they intend to file a complaint against Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over his alleged responsibility for police brutality.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dba18ef0-d9e5-11f1-863b-f351e1b5079d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 14:39:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nacho Doce</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'AI cannot do everything': bullying experts warn against confiding in chatbots</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-one-quarter-of-young-bullying-victims-turning-to-ai-for-help-study-finds</link><description>
As a growing number of victims turn to artificial intelligence for help, experts warn that, while a virtual confidante can offer temporary relief, the focus must be on prevention and support.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">71185a8c-d797-11f1-a35f-45b5729425b2</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:35:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg">© pixabay / Yamu_Jay</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Latest figures show domestic violence still major problem in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-chilling-figures-show-domestic-violence-still-major-problem-in-france</link><description>
French authorities recorded 285,000 victims of domestic violence in 2025, mostly women, representing a 5 percent increase in a year. It comes as lawmakers debate a new law against sexual and gender-based violence that is due to be finalised at the beginning of 2027.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">77dc943a-d92e-11f1-90a5-5193511bd582</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 06:08:15 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg">© Andreea Alexandru / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>‘We’ll get them’: Macron’s private comments on rivals revealed in new book</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-we-ll-get-them-macron-s-private-comments-on-rivals-revealed-in-new-book</link><description>
Private messages exchanged between French President Emmanuel Macron and journalist Françoise Degois over two years have been published in a new book, revealing his views on political rivals, the rise of the far right and his own leadership. The president reportedly learnt of the book’s existence just three days before its release.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ed7d8d46-d8f9-11f1-8648-c35846abfa7a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:07:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg">© AP - Susan Walsh </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French prosecutors investigate €100m cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel banking group</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-prosecutors-investigate-%E2%82%AC100m-cyberattack-on-cr%C3%A9dit-mutuel-banking-group</link><description>
French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a sophisticated cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa involving fraudulent transfers estimated at around €100 million, as the Brittany-based banking group races to recover the stolen funds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d4c86e50-d8f5-11f1-8292-031c66ea2070</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 12:31:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg">AFP - FRED TANNEAU</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>MPs unanimously reject 2027 French budget as political deadlock continues</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-mps-unanimously-reject-2027-budget-as-political-deadlock-deepens</link><description>
France's National Assembly has overwhelmingly rejected the government's draft budget for 2027 after MPs from across the political spectrum voted against a heavily amended version of the legislation, sending the bill to the Senate in its original form and setting the stage for another round of difficult negotiations.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">94610092-d8ec-11f1-83cc-05d8d1a87801</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:19:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg">© AFP/Dimitar Dilkoff</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mass protests sweep France as workers and students demand higher pay and funding</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-unions-join-forces-for-nationwide-strike-as-protests-intensify</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Thursday as workers, students and pensioners joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations demanding higher wages, action on the cost of living and better public services. Nearly 1.6 million people joined the marches, including 350,000 in Paris, the CGT union said. The Interior Ministry gave a much lower nationwide estimate of around 600,000.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d1ac4db2-d847-11f1-8e8e-b39696b484d3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 07:11:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg">© AP Photo/Thibault Camus</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students blockade dozens of high schools in France before nationwide strike</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261103-students-blockade-dozens-of-high-schools-in-france-before-nationwide-strike</link><description>
Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike later this week.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f797ebc-d75d-11f1-9716-917a4357a158</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 12:20:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg">© Matthieu Rondel / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Calls mount to ban French TV channel following racist killing</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261102-calls-mount-to-ban-french-tv-channel-after-racist-killing</link><description>
A petition urging that a French television channel be taken off air gained traction on Monday, after accusations that far-right views it aired contributed to the racist killing of a black man.

      <description><p>New data comes after Republicans’ midterms losses – which were largely seen as a rebuke of the party over high prices</p><p>US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations but still a cooldown in price increases as the cost of gas dipped during the month.</p><p>The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year-over-year inflation figure as part of the consumer price index (CPI), which measures the price of a basket of goods and services, as data was not collected in October 2025 during the government shutdown.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/october-inflation-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Oil prices fall to lowest since August as Trump says Iran war is ‘effectively over’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/oil-prices-fall-donald-trump-iran-war-ftse-100-markets</link>
      <description><p>Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes</p><p>Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/09/trump-iran-war">Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over”</a>.</p><p>Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”. The fall came after a near 6% drop on Monday on signs that the conflict might be nearing an end.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/oil-prices-fall-donald-trump-iran-war-ftse-100-markets">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/06/us-job-growth-october</link>
      <description><p>‘Low-hire, low-fire’ labor market shows sluggish growth but few layoffs, with an interest rate hike expected in December</p><p>The US added 165,000 jobs to the economy in October, a sign of resilience in the labor market amid war in the Middle East and inflation, according to new data released on Friday.</p><p>Economists had said the labor market has been stuck in a “low-hire, low-fire” state, in which job growth is sluggish but layoffs also remain low, but October’s data surpassed economist expectations.       <description><p>Democrats’ success was helped by popular anger over tech, AI and the super rich – life for billionaires could become much more difficult</p><p>The photo of Silicon Valley centibillionaires at Donald Trump’s inauguration – Musk, Bezos and Zuckerberg, front row and side by side – now looks like a hitlist for a blue Congress hellbent on making life difficult for billionaires.</p><p>The picture symbolized at the time the bending of the knee by the richest men in the world to its most powerful, a symbiosis of the ultra-rich. Already unfathomably wealthy, Silicon Valley tycoons believed a Maga-sized public shift to the right would enrich them even more. It did. For several years, while Trump seemed an everlasting kingmaker and AI’s expansion seemed unstoppable, their fortunes ballooned to values beyond comprehension. Elon Musk’s surpassed $1tn.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/05/tech-barons-america-musk-bezos-zuckerberg">Continue reading...</a></description>

Yes,&nbsp;it can be revealed, Kane loved to reward himself after a gruelling 90 minutes with a bag of sweets. “I do like a Haribo,” he said with a smile after the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/29/czechia-england-nations-league-match-report">Nations&nbsp;League win against Czechia</a> in Prague at the end of September.</p><p>No more. At the beginning of last&nbsp;season, Kane took the decision to cut out the naughty treats. After&nbsp;a while, he noticed a difference. He felt sharper; able to&nbsp;sprint more, make a greater number of accelerations. Was it down to this latest entry on the list of personal sacrifices? Or was it a consequence of his broader health regime, the scope of which is mind-blowing?</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/harry-kane-record-england-cap-bone-broth-sweets-ban-acupuncture">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/10/shirt-numbers-tell-story-football-tactical-evolution</link>
      <description><p>In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2026/nov/10/ultimate-1-50-the-male-footballers-best-associated-with-each-squad-number">Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players</a></p></li></ul><p>Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the <em>enganche</em>, the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque.</p><p>But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/10/shirt-numbers-tell-story-football-tactical-evolution">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Armed with an impressive academic record and experience as a rugby fly-half, the teenager is anything but typical</p><p>Josh King is talking with pride about how his mother, Michelle, a university lecturer, has almost finished her PhD in sickle cell disease. The Fulham attacking midfielder, who is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/06/jude-jobe-bellingham-thomas-tuchel-england-croatia-spain-nations-league">in the England squad</a> for the Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain this week, mentions that his father, Steve, is a lawyer and says he might have liked to follow in his footsteps if it had not worked out for him on the pitch.</p><p>King’s background is not that of a typical footballer. He went on to study part-time for A-levels in French, maths and psychology, getting grades of A, C and D – pretty impressive, especially when you consider he sat the exams in a hotel suite in Romania in the summer of last year while playing for England at the European Under-19 Championship.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/cerebral-josh-king-plots-unusual-route-into-tuchels-england-plans">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/football-comes-together-spain-honour-jesus-de-miguel-tenerife</link>
      <description><p>Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them</p><p>In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/feb/17/osasuna-ante-budimir-real-madrid-bellingham-la-liga">than anyone in their history</a> stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.”</p><p>With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/03/tenerife-footballer-jesus-de-miguel-hospital-collision">who died after a collision on the pitch</a> five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/football-comes-together-spain-honour-jesus-de-miguel-tenerife">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title><![CDATA[France 24 - Infos, news & actualités - L'information internationale en direct]]></title><description>France 24 décrypte l’actualité internationale, politique, l’économie, l’environnement, la culture, le sport, en France et à l’international avec analyses, des interviews, des reportages exclusifs, des magazines et des documentaires.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 07:01:04 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/fr/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>Christophe Gleizes détenu depuis 500 jours : le monde du sport maintient le pressing</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261111-christophe-gleizes-d%C3%A9tenu-depuis-500-jours-monde-sport-maintient-pressing-algerie</link><description>
Détenu depuis 500 jours dans une prison algérienne pour "apologie du terrorisme", le grand reporter Christophe Gleizes continue de purger une peine de sept ans malgré une intense mobilisation de ses proches et du monde du football. Dans l'attente d'une grâce présidentielle, ses soutiens multiplient les actions médiatiques pour obtenir sa libération.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e04ca8ac-d780-11f1-9245-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B76M8PZ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e04ca8ac-d780-11f1-9245-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B76M8PZ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ed012a96-d785-11f1-811d-7f5d52fe6427</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 06:08:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e04ca8ac-d780-11f1-9245-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B76M8PZ.jpg">© Franck Fife, AFP</source><dc:creator>Aude MAZOUÉ</dc:creator></item><item><category>Dans la presse</category><title>En Egypte, "l'intensification des atteintes à la liberté de la presse"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/dans-la-presse/20261111-en-egypte-l-intensification-des-atteintes-%C3%A0-la-libert%C3%A9-de-la-presse</link><description>
A la Une de la presse, ce mercredi 11 novembre, la première grève générale, aujourd’hui, en Espagne, depuis 14 ans. L’échec, en France, de la pétition pour la fermeture de la chaîne CNews. La liberté de la presse plus malmenée que jamais en Egypte. De nouvelles révélations sur l’affaire Nvidia. Et deux enquêtes sur des pans méconnus de l’histoire de la Première guerre mondiale, dont la France commémore aujourd’hui l’armistice.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/797ab2e4-dd8f-11f1-87b0-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/10-LE-MONDE-MADA-MASR.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/797ab2e4-dd8f-11f1-87b0-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/10-LE-MONDE-MADA-MASR.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">05117b16-dd91-11f1-b9a4-9d7e58b724be</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 05:30:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Hélène FRADE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Amériques</category><title>Présidentielle au Brésil : Meta écope d'une amende pour traitement inégal entre Lula et Bolsonaro</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/am%C3%A9riques/20261111-presidentielle-bresil-meta-ecope-amende-traitement-inegal-lula-bolsonaro</link><description>
Le Tribunal supérieur électoral du Brésil a infligé mardi au géant des technologies Meta une amende de 7,5 millions de réais (environ 1,2 million d’euros) pour n'avoir pas respecté l'égalité de traitement entre les candidats à la présidentielle Lula et Flavio Bolsonaro. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fc2552f4-cd9e-11f1-a37c-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/AFP-20261014-D39K34J-v1-HighRes-IrelandEuAiSummit.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fc2552f4-cd9e-11f1-a37c-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/AFP-20261014-D39K34J-v1-HighRes-IrelandEuAiSummit.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">49bb619a-dd79-11f1-a8a6-996d9097a303</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 02:40:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fc2552f4-cd9e-11f1-a37c-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/AFP-20261014-D39K34J-v1-HighRes-IrelandEuAiSummit.jpg">© Paul Faith, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>En direct : poursuite des pourparlers entre l'Ukraine et la Russie à Abu Dhabi</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/europe/20261111-en-direct-poursuite-pourparlers-ukraine-russie-abu-dhabi-zelensky-poutine-kushner</link><description>
Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky s'est dit "satisfait" du changement d'approche de Washington dans les pourparlers avec Moscou qui doivent se poursuivre mercredi à Abu Dhabi, insistant toutefois sur la nécessité de garanties de sécurité pour son pays. Suivez notre direct.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/467b32a0-dd77-11f1-9a39-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26314365694784.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/467b32a0-dd77-11f1-9a39-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26314365694784.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">04c9318a-dd78-11f1-86d9-654870f49686</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 02:32:05 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/467b32a0-dd77-11f1-9a39-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26314365694784.jpg">© Altaf Qadri, pool via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Amériques</category><title>En Haïti, le président du Salvador Nayib Bukele mène l'offensive contre les gangs</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/am%C3%A9riques/20261111-haiti-president-salvador-nayib-bukele-offensive-contre-gangs-400-mawozo</link><description>
Le président du Salvador Nayib Bukele affirme que ses soldats ont détruit le "quartier général" de l'un des principaux gangs en Haïti, 400 Mawozo. Plus de 2 000 militaires salvadoriens ont été déployés dans le pays en proie aux violences depuis la fin du mois d'octobre.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f6b96226-dd6e-11f1-8550-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26304751949491.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f6b96226-dd6e-11f1-8550-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26304751949491.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9d5090a0-dd6f-11f1-a2ae-a5e4992b2ac7</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 01:31:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f6b96226-dd6e-11f1-8550-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26304751949491.jpg">© Odelyn Joseph, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Amériques</category><title>Congrès américain : la procédure de destitution contre Pete Hegseth tuée dans l'œuf</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/am%C3%A9riques/20261111-congres-americain-procedure-de-destitution-contre-pete-hegseth-tuee-dans-l-%C5%93uf</link><description>

Un suspect présentant un trouble psychique a été interpellé samedi 7 novembre après l'incendie de l'ancien refuge de montagne d'Adolf Hitler connu comme le Nid d'Aigle, site très touristique du sud de l'Allemagne, les autorités privilégiant la piste d'un incendie volontaire. Depuis, les débats s'enchaînent à propos de sa potentielle restauration. Les précisions de Caroline Du Bled, correspondante France 24 à Berlin.

Les autorités françaises ont désigné le groupe de pirates informatiques iraniens Shahid Kaveh comme responsable des cyberattaques contre les réfrigérateurs de supermarchés. French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efe09190-dcbf-11f1-9487-5f60e87d1ec6</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 04:33:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg">© Abdul Saboor, POOL/AFP/File</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-top-contemporary-french-artist-christian-boltanski-dies-aged-76</link><description>
Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>
Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2534ffb8-8980-11ec-8ce4-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 12:31:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sharon GAFFNEY</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says world leaders have made 'stupid' comments on France riots based on fake AI videos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261021-macron-says-world-leaders-have-made-stupid-comments-on-france-riots-based-on-fake-ai-videos</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>
Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4e47fa4-88f4-11ec-97bf-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 10:43:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png">© FMM Graphic Studio</source><dc:creator>Tracy MCNICOLL</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teen wounds headmaster and teacher after opening fire at French school</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-french-police-arrest-14-year-old-after-two-teaching-staff-wounded-by-hunting-rifle-fire</link><description>
Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">de062bda-c61f-11f1-828c-2d5a86616301</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg">© Lou Benoist, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France 2022: The Choice</category><title>Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/france-2022-the-campaign/20220207-battle-for-the-far-right-zemmour-le-pen-fight-to-steal-each-other-s-thunder</link><description>
As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ecf0724-8861-11ec-862b-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Feb 2022 22:00:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PERELMAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261011-a-profile-of-rapha%C3%ABl-glucksmann-the-man-who-wants-to-be-french-president</link><description>
Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential elections, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Détenu depuis 500 jours dans une prison algérienne pour "apologie du terrorisme", le grand reporter Christophe Gleizes continue de purger une peine de sept ans malgré une intense mobilisation de ses proches et du monde du football. Dans l'attente d'une grâce présidentielle, ses soutiens multiplient les actions médiatiques pour obtenir sa libération.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e04ca8ac-d780-11f1-9245-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B76M8PZ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e04ca8ac-d780-11f1-9245-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B76M8PZ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ed012a96-d785-11f1-811d-7f5d52fe6427</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 06:08:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e04ca8ac-d780-11f1-9245-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B76M8PZ.jpg">© Franck Fife, AFP</source><dc:creator>Aude MAZOUÉ</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Nouvelle journée de mobilisation dans l'éducation, une élue agressée</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261110-nouvelle-journ%C3%A9e-mobilisation-dans-%C3%A9ducation-%C3%A9lue-agress%C3%A9e</link><description>
Les organisations de jeunesse et les enseignants ont à nouveau manifesté mardi lors d'une journée de mobilisation marquée par l'agression d'une élue de Chelles, visée par un jet de bouteille d'essence devant un lycée francilien. Emmanuel Macron a appelé à punir les auteurs "avec la plus grande fermeté"
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/40aa3732-dd44-11f1-bb4a-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T160817Z-1397439590-RC21LOAQ7ENX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/40aa3732-dd44-11f1-bb4a-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T160817Z-1397439590-RC21LOAQ7ENX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1099368c-dd45-11f1-b9fb-ebd614e9aa03</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 20:35:52 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/40aa3732-dd44-11f1-bb4a-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T160817Z-1397439590-RC21LOAQ7ENX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Stéphane Mahe, REUTERS</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Éric Zemmour confirme sa candidature à la présidentielle pour "enrayer le déclin"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261110-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-confirme-candidature-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-enrayer-d%C3%A9clin</link><description>

Le procès de trois policiers, accusés d'avoir roué de coups le producteur de musique noir Michel Zecler en novembre 2020, s'est ouvert ce lundi 9 novembre.
